notes: Concise original summaries of publicly documented creator stories. Figures are attributed and marked self-reported where applicable. 'unknown' means the source did not state it. Many records come from Selar's own blog, which is promotional content for the platform; see research-limitations.md.

fields.name: creator or organisation as publicly documented
fields.country: only when stated or clearly implied by the source; otherwise 'unknown'
fields.region: Nigerian state/city only when verified by the source; otherwise 'unknown'
fields.lessons: list of lessons relevant to the game
fields.sources: list of {title, publisher, url, published, accessed}

stories.name: WakaWaka Doctor
stories.startingSituation: Working two jobs for about ₦200,000 a month before a job abroad led to years of travel. A YouTube video about moving to France drew attention and followers began asking for study-abroad and visa guidance.
stories.strategy: Turned recurring audience questions into an ebook, then added consultations through a travel agency and a paid membership community.
channels: Social media with a single store link
stories.revenueModel: Ebook sales (direct and affiliate-driven), consultation fees, membership fees.

reportedOutcomes.claim: Sold his first 1,000 books in about four months.
reportedOutcomes.attribution: WakaWaka Doctor, quoted by Selar blog

challenges: Distributing the ebook to a geographically spread audience
lessons: Audience questions reveal product ideas
A single checkout link reduces repetitive selling
Affiliates can extend reach
View-only delivery limits copying
Memberships and consulting extend one topic into several offers

sources.title: WakaWaka Doctor case study

stories.evidenceNotes: Platform-published case study; outcome is self-reported and unverified. No prices were given.

stories.name: Omobolaji Ajibare (Social Media Oga)
stories.category: Knowledge creator / social media educator / community builder
stories.startingSituation: Lost a 9-to-5 job after probation, then COVID-19 disrupted a later role. Had managed social media since university without treating it as a career.
stories.strategy: Gave away a free slide PDF as a lead magnet, sold low-priced classes, then a toolkit with tickets and a paid community; teased launches on Instagram Stories.
products: Free PDF from a training (lead magnet)
stories.revenueModel: Digital products, classes, tickets and paid community training, alongside freelance work.

reportedOutcomes.claim: First class sold to five buyers at ₦3,000 (about ₦15,000).
Over 3,000 people accessed the free PDF.
Over 150 toolkit tickets sold; over 1 million (currency unstated) in the first month.
'Over 6 million' in tracked earnings from digital products; does not closely track expenses.
Community of about 3,800 members.

challenges: Wants dollar income without registering abroad
An account with about 35k followers was taken down
lessons: Free lead magnets build a list
Start with small, cheap offers and grow
Tease launches to a warm audience
Rest to avoid burnout
Build strategy on your own audience

sources.title: #CreatorStories: The Social Media Oga story

stories.evidenceNotes: Self-reported figures in a platform blog; creator states she does not track all expenses, so 'earnings' is closer to revenue than profit.

stories.name: Felix Ohaeri
stories.startingSituation: Earlier fruit-juice and e-commerce ventures failed. Earned a first ₦1,000 helping someone post content, then did graphic design before moving into digital marketing and Facebook ads for clients.
stories.strategy: Picked a trending, high-demand topic (AI), ran a two-day live class, converted it to a pre-recorded course, then sold it on a checkout platform supported by paid ads.
products: Magnetic AI Course (AI for marketers and teams)
stories.revenueModel: Course sales funded by reinvested ad spend.

reportedOutcomes.claim: Roughly ₦10 million in sales in one month.
45–55 new students a day on average, up to 70 at weekends, from nine countries.
Spends about a third of earnings on marketing for 'about three times return'.

challenges: Previous hosting couldn't handle student volume
Lack of time to build a website
lessons: Timing and demand matter
Measure return on ad spend and reinvest when it works
Master one niche before expanding
Previous failures can precede success

sources.title: How Felix Ohaeri used Selar to make 10 million in a month

stories.evidenceNotes: Promotional case study. Figures self-reported. Location not explicitly stated (naira figures used). An outlier result; not a representative benchmark.

stories.name: Ene Annabelle Ajogwu (Passive Income Anna)
stories.startingSituation: Lost savings in a Ponzi scheme, had a poor network-marketing experience and lost a large content page. In 2023 she was in severe financial difficulty.
stories.strategy: Made a first ebook in Canva in under two hours, then promoted her own and other creators' products with very frequent organic posting, webinars and practical classes.
products: Ebook on dressing and looking better
Affiliate promotion of other creators' products
channels: Instagram organic content (5–8 posts a day)
stories.revenueModel: Own digital products plus affiliate commissions.

reportedOutcomes.claim: First ebook sold six copies on launch day.
Best-seller rose from about 100 to over 600 sales in four weeks after more intensive marketing.
First ₦1,000,000 in sales around February 2024; body text confirms ₦100m reached; headline claims over ₦200m in two years.
An AI product made fewer than five sales on launch day.

challenges: Repeated Instagram suspensions she attributes to spam-like phrases
lessons: A weak launch can be improved with consistent promotion
Consistency and visibility
Address specific audience pain points
Platform rules can restrict reach suddenly
Affiliate promotion multiplies the value of content

sources.title: From Tears on a Bathroom Floor to Over ₦200m in Two Years with Selar: The Passive Income Anna Story

stories.country: Nigeria (implied by naira figures and cities)
stories.startingSituation: Sold makeup at school, then ran a dropshipping beauty business.
stories.strategy: After failures, rebuilt trust through generous handling of a faulty skincare batch; now runs several product and service businesses with documented systems.

challenges: Bereavement, theft of materials and loss of workspace
